articles.title: Iran Just Fired Missiles at Three Ships in the Strait of Hormuz. India Lifted Its Emergency Gas Curbs Two Days Ago.
articles.excerpt: The IRGC attacked a Qatari LNG tanker and a Saudi oil tanker during Khamenei's funeral procession, threatening the ceasefire that let India's energy supply chain breathe again. Oil jumped 2.5 per cent within hours.
articles.image_caption: An LNG tanker at sea — vessels like these carry the bulk of India's gas imports through the Strait of Hormuz
articles.nri_angle: India imports 65 per cent of its LNG through the Strait of Hormuz and 9 million Indians live in the Gulf states directly exposed to the conflict's fallout.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Told 300,000 Indian Families Their Children Are American. The Fight Isn't Over.
articles.excerpt: A 6-3 ruling strikes down Trump's birthright citizenship order — but the administration is already plotting its next move, and a separate ruling on nationwide injunctions complicates the legal landscape.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families on H-1B visas and in green card backlogs were among those most directly threatened by the order — their U.S.-born children's citizenship was at stake.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Giants Are Heading Into a 'Perfect Storm.' Their 200,000 Workers in America Feel It First.
articles.excerpt: AI is eating the $315 billion industry's traditional business model. TCS reports Thursday, and nine brokerages are bracing for another grim quarter.
articles.image_caption: Infosys campus in Bangalore — the company reports Q1 earnings later this month amid mounting AI disruption concerns.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT firms are the largest H-1B sponsors in the U.S.; a structural downturn affects visa sponsorship, hiring pipelines, and career prospects for 200,000+ Indian tech workers in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Cyber Agency Is Using Anthropic's AI to Hunt Bugs in Government Code. India's $108 Billion IT Industry Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: CISA's deployment of the Mythos model to scan federal software for vulnerabilities signals a shift that could reshape the government IT services market dominated by Indian outsourcing firms.
articles.image_caption: The CISA seal — the US federal cyber defence agency now deploying AI for code audits
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT giants like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro earn tens of billions annually from US government contracts — AI-powered code auditing could reshape the services market they dominate, while Indian-Americans in cybersecurity roles watch the Anthropic-Washington standoff from the inside.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Is in Indonesia With a Missile Deal. Then He'll Face a Million Indians in Melbourne and Anti-Indian Sentiment in New Zealand.
articles.excerpt: A six-day, three-nation tour through the Asia-Pacific puts defence exports, temple diplomacy, and diaspora politics on the same itinerary.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an official portrait
articles.nri_angle: Nearly 4 million Indians live across Indonesia, Australia, and New Zealand — this tour directly addresses their security, cultural identity, and community standing in countries where the diaspora is both growing and under scrutiny.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Wants to Kill Day 1 CPT. Tens of Thousands of Indian Professionals Have No Plan B.
articles.excerpt: A proposed rule eliminating 'Duration of Status' for F-1 visas would shut the last legal workaround for Indians trapped in the H-1B lottery — and could trigger a talent exodus from America's AI workforce.
articles.image_caption: A USCIS facility — Washington is moving to eliminate Day 1 CPT, a pathway used by tens of thousands of Indian professionals (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: US Department of Homeland Security proposed rule (May 2026)

articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian professionals who relied on Day 1 CPT after H-1B lottery rejections face potential deportation or forced return if the proposed rule eliminates their last legal workaround.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Just Cut 4,800 Jobs to Pay for AI. Its 20,000 Indian Employees Are Watching.
articles.excerpt: The company's fourth round of layoffs in eighteen months guts the Xbox division and deepens a pattern that is sending thousands of Indian tech workers home from the US.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of Microsoft's Redmond campus in Washington state
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft employs over 20,000 people in India and thousands more Indian professionals on US work visas; the AI-driven layoff wave is accelerating reverse migration and reshaping career calculus for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hamas Just Dissolved Its Government in Gaza. India Stayed Out of the Peace Plan — and Has Its Reasons.
articles.excerpt: The militant group's symbolic move pressures Israel to act on a stalled US-brokered deal. India's refusal to join Trump's Board of Peace reflects a calculation that runs through 8.5 million NRIs in the Gulf.
articles.image_caption: Damaged residential buildings in the Gaza Strip during the conflict
articles.nri_angle: India's refusal to join the Gaza peace framework is driven partly by the need to protect 8.5 million Indian workers across the Gulf, whose safety and livelihoods depend on regional stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NATO's Biggest Summit in Years Starts Tomorrow. India Isn't at the Table — but It's on Every Agenda.
articles.excerpt: Ankara will host 32 leaders, €70 billion in Ukraine aid, a defence industry bonanza, and the Iran question. Every outcome touches India's strategic calculus.
articles.image_caption: NATO headquarters in Brussels — alliance leaders are gathering this week for a pivotal summit in Ankara (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NATO defence spending reshapes the job market for diaspora defence and tech professionals, while the Iran outcome directly determines oil prices, rupee strength, and economic stability for NRI families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Just Fell to Pre-War Levels. For India, the Breathing Room Is Enormous.
articles.excerpt: OPEC+ keeps adding supply, Brent is back below $72, and India's inflation, rupee and fiscal maths are all improving at once. But the ceasefire holding it together is fragile.
articles.image_caption: An oil refinery at dusk — falling crude prices are delivering macroeconomic relief across India
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper oil strengthens the rupee, protects family purchasing power, and makes remittances go further — the single most direct macroeconomic benefit for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Made Gasoline Is Reaching Russia Through Traders. New Delhi Says It Has Nothing to Do With It.
articles.excerpt: As Ukrainian drone strikes cripple a third of Russia's refining capacity, fuel from Nayara Energy — 49% owned by Rosneft — is sailing north via intermediaries. India's oil minister insists no Indian company is selling directly. The distinction may not hold for long.
articles.image_caption: An Indian oil refinery — Reuters reports that India-made gasoline is reaching Russia through trader intermediaries (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India-Russia fuel trade complicates the India-US trade deal that directly affects five million Indian Americans and Indian exporters.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Says a Historic India-US Trade Deal Is 'Very Very Close.' India Says Not Until It Gets Better Terms Than Pakistan.
articles.excerpt: At the USISPF summit in Washington, American officials project imminent success on a $500 billion trade target. But India's Commerce Minister has drawn an unmovable red line: no deal unless Indian tariffs fall below Pakistan's. The gap is 2.5 percentage points — and it could take months to close.
articles.image_caption: Wikipedia portrait of Vinay Mohan Kwatra
articles.nri_angle: The India-US trade deal directly affects five million Indian Americans, Indian IT firms operating in the US, and the regulatory environment for Global Capability Centres.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The July Visa Bulletin Just Shut the Door on India's EB-2 Green Cards. It Will Not Reopen Until October.
articles.excerpt: EB-2 India declared unavailable for the rest of FY2026, EB-1 retrogressed by two months, and EB-5 unreserved also shut — the worst mid-year bulletin for Indian professionals in years.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. State Department building in Washington, D.C. — the July 2026 Visa Bulletin has retrogressed EB-2 India to unavailable (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US face frozen green card applications until October, with EB-2 declared unavailable and EB-1 retrogressing — the worst mid-year bulletin in years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants Access to Anthropic's Most Powerful AI. Washington Is Listening — Carefully.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi is in talks to use Anthropic's Project Glasswing to stress-test India's critical digital infrastructure, as both countries navigate the geopolitics of frontier AI.
articles.image_caption: Frontier AI models are at the heart of US-India technology negotiations (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI professionals work at the heart of America's frontier AI companies; the US-India partnership on model access will determine how freely their expertise flows between both ecosystems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Accounts Just Went Live. For Indian-American Families, the Math Is Extraordinarily Good.
articles.excerpt: The government's new $1,000 seed investment program launched on July 4. With Indian Americans among the highest-earning groups in the U.S., their families are uniquely positioned to maximize it — but only if they act fast.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Treasury Department building in Washington, D.C., which oversees the new Trump Accounts program
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families — among the highest-earning in the U.S. — are uniquely positioned to maximize Trump Accounts, but eligibility requires U.S. citizenship, creating a sharp distinction for H-1B families with foreign-born vs. American-born children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hundreds of Masked White Nationalists Marched Through Washington on America's 250th Birthday. They Chanted 'Reclaim America.'
articles.excerpt: The Patriot Front's flash-mob march near the US Capitol came hours after Trump called immigrants a 'communist menace' at Mount Rushmore — a jarring backdrop for the 4.8 million Indian Americans celebrating the Fourth of July.
articles.image_caption: Patriot Front members march in formation through Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: White nationalist group marches through the US capital on July 4, directly challenging the belonging of immigrant communities including the 4.8 million Indian Americans who call America home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Britain Is About to Get Its Seventh Prime Minister in a Decade. The 1.8 Million Indians There Are Watching Closely.
articles.excerpt: Andy Burnham is expected to enter Downing Street by July 20 — five days after the India-UK trade deal goes live. His domestic-first agenda could reshape life for Britain's Indian diaspora.
articles.image_caption: Andy Burnham, the incoming British Prime Minister, at an event in August 2024
articles.nri_angle: Britain's next PM takes over just as the India-UK trade deal goes live, with direct implications for 1.8 million NRIs on social security portability, worker mobility, and the future of India-UK relations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
